- **Defaults** are what a run gets when the flag is omitted: `off` for a

## `run-ingestion`

Unified Knowledge Graph RAG on AWS: parse documents and build the knowledge graph and indexes the selected methodologies read

Guide: [Ingestion](../guides/ingest.md). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--source-directory` | — | Directory of the source documents to process; required unless --verify-metadata (falls back to the UKR_SOURCE_DIRECTORY env var). |
| `--output-directory` | — | Export each parsed document as <stem>.json to this directory for inspection (processing.document_parsing.target_directory; no export when omitted; must not be the source directory). |
| `--cache-directory` | — | Directory of the pipeline cache and intermediate results (default: cache). |
| `--force-rebuild` | off | Recompute every stage, ignoring the cached stage outputs, the stored extraction records and the LLM response cache: every model call and embedding is paid again (the caches are rewritten with the new outputs). |
| `--s3-sync` | off | Synchronize the cache with Amazon S3 (needs --s3-bucket-name or aws.s3.bucket_name). |
| `--s3-bucket-name` | — | Amazon S3 bucket for cache synchronization with --s3-sync (default: aws.s3.bucket_name). |
| `--s3-prefix` | `pipeline-runs` | S3 object key prefix for organizing cache files (default: pipeline-runs). |
| `--pipeline-id` | — | Identifier of the pipeline run to resume or inspect (falls back to the UKR_PIPELINE_ID env var). It names the run's cache directory and S3 prefix, so it takes letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only: up to 128 characters, starting with a letter or digit, with no '..'. |
| `--resume-from-stage` | — | Pipeline stage to resume from, by name (case-insensitive; requires --pipeline-id); an unknown name is a usage error. |
| `--verify-metadata` | off | Verify the integrity of the run's pipeline metadata (needs --pipeline-id); exits non-zero when it is corrupt or the run is not found. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | off | Answer yes to confirmation prompts (continuing after a failed integrity check, or a reset that asks first, as --confirm-reset does, or a mass deletion, as --confirm-deletions does). Without it, a prompt that cannot be asked because stdin is not a terminal fails the run. |
| `--confirm-reset` | off | Answer yes to the question of an indexing.reset run that drops another source scope's seed graph documents, or, from a corpus of seed graphs alone, another scope's documents, and of a run with incremental indexing off that rebuilds a non-empty index from the seed graphs alone; nothing else (falls back to the UKR_CONFIRM_RESET env var: 1, true or yes). Without it (or --yes), the question is asked on the terminal, and the run stops (exit 1) when stdin is not one. |
| `--confirm-deletions` | off | Answer yes to the question of an incremental run that would delete more than indexing.max_deletion_share of its source scope's documents (their files are gone from the corpus); nothing else (falls back to the UKR_CONFIRM_DELETIONS env var: 1, true or yes). Without it (or --yes), the question is asked on the terminal, and the run stops (exit 1) before it writes when stdin is not one. |
| `--confirm-integrity` | off | Answer yes to the question of a run that resumes a --pipeline-id whose inputs changed since its stages ran (or whose cache is incomplete): continue, recomputing those stages; nothing else. Without it (or --yes), the question is asked on the terminal, and the run stops (exit 1) when stdin is not one. |
| `--continue-on-error` | off | Keep going when a stage fails. When an artifact stage (translation through community detection) crashes, every document of the run is recorded FAILED, so the next incremental run processes them again. |
| `--enabled-stages` | — | Comma-separated list of pipeline stages to enable (e.g., 'DOCUMENT_PARSING,TEXT_CHUNKING'). If not specified, all stages are enabled. |
| `--metrics-sink` | `none` | Where to forward pipeline metrics: 'none' (default) or 'cloudwatch' (CloudWatch EMF to stdout, auto-extracted by CloudWatch Logs, with an Environment dimension when UKR_METRICS_ENVIRONMENT is set; pipeline_id is a log property, not a dimension). A stage's metrics are emitted when it finishes and only by the run that executed it, so a resumed run does not repeat restored stages' counts. |
| `--retire-source-scope` `SCOPE` | — | Incremental runs: treat every doc-status record of this former source scope (in this run's index namespace) as deleted, removing its exclusive graph and vector content. Use it once after moving a corpus, with the old absolute source directory or former document_parsing.source_scope value (a value that is not a URI is also tried as a path resolved like --source-directory; a bare value whose name and path readings both have records stops the run: use ./ or an absolute path). Repeatable; added to indexing.retire_source_scopes. Never this run's own scope. |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--suffix` | — | Index suffix (namespace) the run writes: processing.document_parsing.index_value (default: the config's, else 'default'). Query it with run-rag/run-eval --suffix. |
| `--methodologies` `LIST` | — | Comma-separated methodologies to build (graphrag, lightrag, hipporag, raptor): indexing.methodologies. |
| `--reset` | off | Rebuild the namespace from the whole corpus instead of applying a delta (indexing.reset: true for this run only, so a config file need not be edited back). |

## `run-rag`

Unified Knowledge Graph RAG on AWS: answer a question (or, with --mode search, retrieve) from the knowledge graph and indexes run-ingestion built, with the GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG or RAPTOR strategies

Guide: [Querying](../guides/query.md). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--query`, `-q` | — | Answer one query; give this or --interactive (exactly one). |
| `--interactive`, `-i` | off | Launch interactive chat mode for continuous conversation (always 'rag' mode, memory on; not with --output-format json). |
| `--mode` | `rag` | Set the execution mode: 'rag' for full generation, 'search' for retrieval only (a single --query only; --interactive always generates). |
| `--conversation-id` | — | Name the conversation. Memory is kept in this process only: it carries over between --interactive turns, not between separate run-rag invocations. |
| `--suffix` | — | Index suffix to query (default: the config's processing.document_parsing.index_value, as ingestion writes, else 'default'); must match the index_value the corpus was ingested with. |
| `--search-strategy` | `auto` | Choose the search strategy. One of `auto`, `drift`, `global`, `local`, `simple`, `mix`, `hybrid`, `naive`, `iterative`, `ppr`, `tree`, `structured`. |
| `--search-type` | `hybrid` | Search method: hybrid (default) fuses a lexical (BM25) and a vector (embedding kNN) search of each index, lexical and vector run one of them alone. The lexical side searches the first 150 words of the question (a Hangul, Han or Kana character counts as a word) and, on OpenSearch, tolerates typos only in questions of up to 10 words with no Hangul, Han or Kana; the vector side embeds the whole question. |
| `--top-k` | `10` | Set the maximum number of search results (times --retrieval-multiplier; default 10). |
| `--retrieval-multiplier` | `1` | Widen the search N times: each index and graph expansion fetches up to top-k x N candidates and the fused list keeps up to top-k x N for the reranker and the context budget, at the cost of larger searches (default 1). |
| `--disable-query-processing` | off | Skip query translation and the query-side entity and keyword extraction (no LLM call before retrieval). mix and hybrid then have no high- or low-level keywords: a question shorter than search.lightrag_search.raw_query_fallback_max_len characters is searched as its own low-level keyword, a longer one retrieves no entities or relationships. |
| `--filters` | — | Attribute filters as space-separated 'key:value' pairs (a repeated --filters adds its pairs); a boolean or numeric field takes its type's value (in_schema:false, rank:2). |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--metrics-sink` | `none` | Where to send query metrics: 'none' (default) or 'cloudwatch' (CloudWatch EMF to stdout: query_latency_ms and the outcome counts query_failed, query_degraded and query_abstained of each --mode rag query under unified_kg_rag/query, with an Environment dimension when UKR_METRICS_ENVIRONMENT is set and the Strategy that ran; not with --output-format json). |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | off | Show more of each result: the query processing, every source (or search hit) with its score and text, and the metrics; with --output-format json, also an answer's search_results.results (the logs: --log-level). |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |

## `run-eval`

Unified Knowledge Graph RAG on AWS: evaluate retrieval and answers on a dataset, and compare strategies

Guide: [Evaluation](../guides/evaluate.md). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-path` | — | Path to the unified evaluation data file (JSON format), containing both questions and ground truths. Accepts a local path or an s3://bucket/key URI (downloaded before the run). This or --from-results is required. |
| `--from-results` `PATH` | — | Rebuild the comparison from saved runs instead of answering: result directories (read with their run subdirectories) or evaluation_results_*.json files (with their reports and summary next to them). A strategy's runs from several run-eval invocations are refused without --pool-runs. No answer is generated and no store is queried; --pairwise-judge re-judges the saved answers (with --judge-model, another model). The strategies compare in --search-strategy order when given, else in the order the oldest run listed them. Local paths only. |
| `--rescore` `DATASET` | — | With --from-results, score the saved answers again with this run's evaluators (--evaluators, evaluation.*: answer_match's span and normalization, the citation metrics, the LLM judges, which are called again) instead of comparing the scores they hold, and save the re-scored runs in this run's directory. The gold answers are those saved with each answer, or DATASET's (a run-eval dataset whose items pair by query id: their answer, aliases, metadata and expectations replace the saved ones). No answer is generated and no store is queried. |
| `--baseline-results` `PATH` | — | Compare against an earlier run: its saved results (directories or evaluation_results_*.json files) become the baselines, as 'baseline:<strategy>', and each strategy of this run, or of --from-results, is compared with the baseline of the same strategy (with the earlier run's first strategy, and a warning, when it has none). Refused when the runs scored exact_match and token_f1 with different answer_scoring settings. |
| `--pool-runs` | off | Pool the saved runs of one strategy as its repeats although they come from several run-eval invocations, or ran with different settings (a warning names them). Without it --from-results and --baseline-results refuse such runs (exit 2): list the result files, or the run subdirectory, of one invocation. |
| `--fail-if` `MEASURE:STAT<OP>VALUE` | — | Regression gate, repeatable: exit 1 when a compared strategy's paired delta against the baseline meets the condition, or has no delta of MEASURE. MEASURE is an <evaluator>/<metric> of deltas_vs_baseline (abstention/recall and abstention/precision with unanswerable items) or a cost measure (usage/llm_calls, usage/input_tokens, usage/output_tokens, usage/total_tokens, usage/cost_usd, latency/response_time_seconds); STAT is mean_delta, ci_low or ci_high, or adjusted for the many deltas read (--primary-metric): adjusted_ci_low, adjusted_ci_high, p_value or adjusted_p_value; OP is <, <=, > or >=. Example: answer_match/token_f1:adjusted_ci_high<-0.02. Needs a comparison (two strategies or --baseline-results). |
| `--judge-model` `MODEL_ID` | — | Model of the LLM judges for this run (models.roles.evaluation): the pairwise judge and the ragas/assertion evaluators. |
| `--output-directory` | — | Directory to save evaluation results (default: evaluation.outputs_directory), in a subdirectory of its own per run-eval invocation, run_<timestamp>_<id> (evaluation.run_subdirectories). Accepts a local path or an s3://bucket/prefix/ URI (results are uploaded after the run; a failed upload exits non-zero). |
| `--suffix` | — | Index suffix to query (default: the config's processing.document_parsing.index_value, as ingestion writes, else 'default'); must match the index_value the corpus was ingested with. |
| `--search-strategy` | `auto` | Search strategy, or a comma-separated list (e.g. local,mix,global) to answer the same queries with each and compare them pairwise against the first. Give the flag once: a second one is a usage error. |
| `--search-type` | `hybrid` | Search method: hybrid (default) fuses a lexical (BM25) and a vector (embedding kNN) search of each index, lexical and vector run one of them alone. The lexical side searches the first 150 words of the question (a Hangul, Han or Kana character counts as a word) and, on OpenSearch, tolerates typos only in questions of up to 10 words with no Hangul, Han or Kana; the vector side embeds the whole question. |
| `--top-k` | `10` | Set the maximum number of search results (times --retrieval-multiplier; default 10). |
| `--retrieval-multiplier` | `1` | Widen the search N times: each index and graph expansion fetches up to top-k x N candidates and the fused list keeps up to top-k x N for the reranker and the context budget, at the cost of larger searches (default 1). |
| `--evaluators` `NAME[,NAME...]` | — | Evaluators that score this run, comma-separated (default: evaluation.enabled_evaluators, answer_match,retrieval,graph_aware). The LLM judges are opt-in: ragas (the eval extra; several judge calls per answer, one per context for context_precision) and assertion (evaluation.assertion_trials calls per answer). |
| `--repeats` | `1` | Answer and score the dataset this many times per strategy; the comparison averages each query over the repeats and reports the run-to-run spread (default 1). |
| `--primary-metric` `EVALUATOR/METRIC` | — | The comparison's primary metric, declared in advance (default: evaluation.primary_metric, else answer_match/answer_contains when scored): adjusted only over the compared strategies, while every other metric's delta is Holm-adjusted over all of them (adjusted_p_value, adjusted_ci_low/high, which --fail-if can read). |
| `--run-order` | — | How the runs of a comparison are answered (default: evaluation.run_order, 'interleaved'): every query by every run before the next query, the runs' order alternating (ABBA), so latency deltas do not measure time; or 'sequential', one run after another. |
| `--repeat-extractions` | — | With --repeats, whether each repeat extracts the query's entities and keywords again (default: evaluation.repeat_extractions, 'resample': repeat_stdev includes the extraction's variance, at one set of fast-model extraction calls per query and repeat) or reuses the first repeat's ('reuse'). |
| `--pairwise-judge` | off | With two or more strategies, also judge each strategy's answers against the first's with an LLM (comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment, directness; both orders) using models.roles.evaluation. |
| `--pairwise-mode` | — | How --pairwise-judge reads the two answers (default: evaluation.pairwise_mode, 'standard'). 'differential' first splits them into shared and unique statements with models.roles.pairwise_overlap (fast tier, one call per pair) and judges the unique statements only, so shared content and the length it adds earn neither answer credit. Both modes report win rates per answer-length bucket. |
| `--pairwise-repeats` | — | Which repeats --pairwise-judge judges (default: evaluation.pairwise_repeats, 'first'): the first repeat's answers, or 'all', repeat r against repeat r (the judge's calls times --repeats; each query's repeats averaged first). |
| `--closed-book` | off | Also answer every question with the answer model alone, no retrieval (the 'closed_book' arm, compared with the first strategy like another strategy and judged by --pairwise-judge): its scores bound what the model knows without the corpus. One answer call per question and repeat; its retrieval and context metrics score an empty source list, and --fail-if skips it. |
| `--arm` `NAME=OVERLAY[,suffix=SUFFIX][,aa=true]` | — | A configuration arm, repeatable: answer the dataset again with the config under OVERLAY (a YAML mapping merged over it, as a config file is validated; its evaluation section is the run's), as a chain of its own, with each --search-strategy. Its runs are labelled <strategy>@NAME and compared with the same strategy's base run, interleaved with it (--run-order); the arms' deltas are Holm-adjusted in families of their own (arm_primary, arm_secondary, arm_cost, arm_pairwise), apart from the strategies'. The run manifest records the overlay's path and sha256. suffix= queries another index namespace with the arm. An arm whose resolved config equals the run's (cache sizes aside) on its own index, or one given aa=true, is an A/A arm: its deltas are the noise floor, left out of Holm and of --fail-if. |
| `--max-failure-rate` | `1.0` | Exit non-zero when the fraction of queries whose answer generation failed, the fraction of attempted values of any metric that failed, the fraction of reranked queries whose rerank call failed (the fused order kept), or the fraction of answers a retrieval step failure degraded, exceeds this value (0.0-1.0). Skipped metrics do not count. Default 1.0 = fail only when all queries, all attempts of a metric, or all of those, failed. |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

## `run-visualization`

Render graph visualizations from exported data (no ingestion).

Guide: [Visualization](../guides/visualize.md).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-path` | — | Path to exported visualization-data JSON (default: the newest visualization_data.json under graph.visualization.outputs_directory, outputs/visualization and --cache-directory, of --suffix's namespace when given). |
| `--suffix` | — | Index namespace whose newest export to render, without --data-path (the name run-ingestion --suffix wrote it under). |
| `--cache-directory` | `cache` | The run-ingestion cache directory searched without --data-path (default: cache). |
| `--output-directory` | `visualization_outputs` | Directory to write visualization files. |
| `--renderers` `RENDERER` | — | Renderers to run. Available: interactive, static (default: all of them, leaving out with a warning one whose extra is not installed; a renderer named here needs its extra). |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

## `run-describe`

Describe an index namespace (methodologies, servable strategies, indices, build record, registry) and optionally export its graph.

Guide: [Inspect and export](../guides/inspect.md). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--suffix` | — | Index suffix to describe (default: the config's processing.document_parsing.index_value, else 'default'). |
| `--output-path` | — | Also export the namespace's graph to this file (entities, relationships, communities, claims, with the text units and documents they cite). An existing file is refused unless --force, and so are the --config-path file and the schema file the config loads, always. |
| `--force` | off | Let --output-path replace an existing file (never the --config-path file or the schema file the config loads). |
| `--export-format` | `jsonl` | Export format: jsonl (one record per line, every stored field but the vectors) or graphml (entities as nodes, relationships as edges, communities as nodes linked to their parent). |
| `--max-items` | — | Export at most this many items of each kind (default: all). |
| `--include-text` | off | Export each text unit's text too (jsonl only). |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

## `run-prompt-tuning`

Generate domain-adapted custom_prompts from a corpus sample.

Guide: [Domain adaptation](../guides/domain-adaptation.md#prompt-tuning-run-prompt-tuning). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--source-directory` | required | Directory of documents to sample (.txt/.md plus every format run-ingestion parses, e.g. .pdf). |
| `--output-path` | `tuned_prompts.yaml` | Where to write the tuned custom_prompts YAML. An existing file is refused unless --force, and so are the --config-path file and the schema file the config loads, always. |
| `--schema-out` `PATH` | — | Also write an extraction schema draft (.yaml/.yml): the profile's entity types (the configured ones when the config declares them) and the relationship types the tuning examples use most, for schema_source: {kind: file, path: PATH} with schema_mode: align. Every type and pattern the config declares is kept, with its description and IRI. An existing file is refused unless --force, and so are the --config-path file and the schema file the config loads, always: write the draft elsewhere and merge it. |
| `--force` | off | Let --output-path and --schema-out replace an existing file (never the --config-path file or the schema file the config loads). |
| `--max-docs` | `20` | Max documents to sample (at least 1). |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

## `prepare-benchmark`

Prepare a public benchmark (MuSiQue) as a corpus directory and a run-eval dataset, generate questions and assertions from your corpus (assertions), or generate a synthetic structural benchmark for the structured strategy (structural)

Guide: [Benchmarks](../guides/benchmarks.md).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `benchmark` | required | Benchmark to prepare: musique, assertions (questions and assertions generated from --source-directory), or structural (a generated procurement world: corpus/, seed/structural.jsonl, structural-config.yaml and graph-structure questions with gold answers computed over the generated graph). |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

### `prepare-benchmark musique`

Prepare MuSiQue (downloaded at run time, or a local copy) as a corpus directory and a run-eval dataset.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--output-directory` | required | Directory for corpus/ and eval_data.json (corpus/ must be new or empty). |
| `--seed` | `0` | Sampling seed (default 0). |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--data-path` | — | Local official JSONL of the answerable questions (e.g. musique_ans_v1.0_dev.jsonl from the official download; a musique_full_v1.0_*.jsonl supplies its answerable half, labelled musique-full-answerable, and with --unanswerable and no --unanswerable-data-path the unanswerable questions too); default: download the answerable dev split. |
| `--unanswerable-data-path` | — | Local musique_full_v1.0_*.jsonl to draw the --unanswerable questions from (the answerable ones still come from --data-path or the default download); default: the --data-path file when it is a full file, else download the full dev split. |
| `--limit` | — | Number of answerable questions to sample (default: all 2,417 of dev). |
| `--unanswerable` `N` | — | Also write N unanswerable questions of the full split (metadata.answerable: false), leaving out any whose answerable twin is sampled or whose removed supporting paragraph's exact text is in the pooled corpus; the counts are reported (default: none). |
| `--hops` `HOPS` | — | Hop counts to sample from: a list (3,4) filters both answerable and unanswerable questions; quotas (2=50,3=50,4=100) draw exactly that many answerable questions per hop count, instead of --limit (default: every hop count, sampled as one pool). |

### `prepare-benchmark assertions`

Generate questions and assertions from your corpus.

Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--output-directory` | required | Directory for corpus/ and eval_data.json (corpus/ must be new or empty). |
| `--seed` | `0` | Sampling seed of the text units (default 0). |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--source-directory` | — | assertions: directory of .txt/.md files to generate from (the corpus you ingest); required for assertions. |
| `--questions-per-class` | `10` | assertions: questions to keep per class (default 10). |
| `--classes` | `data_local`, `data_global`, `data_linked`, `activity_local`, `activity_global` | assertions: comma-separated question classes (default all: data_local,data_global,data_linked,activity_local,activity_global); only the data_* classes get assertions. |
| `--clusters` | `20` | assertions: k-means clusters of the text units (default 20). |
| `--units-per-cluster` | `8` | assertions: text units in each cluster's sample (default 8). |
| `--unit-tokens` | `600` | assertions: estimated tokens per text unit (default 600). |
| `--max-units` | `3000` | assertions: text units sampled (with --seed) and embedded (default 3000). |
| `--max-assertions` | `10` | assertions: assertions kept per question (default 10). |
| `--language` | — | assertions: language of the questions and assertions (default: processing.translation.source_language). One of `ar`, `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `he`, `hi`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt`, `ru`, `th`, `vi`, `zh`. |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |

### `prepare-benchmark structural`

Generate a synthetic procurement world, its seed graph and graph-structure questions for the structured strategy.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--output-directory` | required | Directory for corpus/ and eval_data.json (corpus/ must be new or empty). |
| `--seed` | `0` | The generated world's seed (default 0). |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--size` | `small` | The world's size (small: 8 vendors, 6 buyers, up to 4 questions a template; medium: 40 vendors, 30 buyers, up to 25 a template; large: 400 vendors, 300 buyers, so a seed-filtered count scans past search.structured.max_scan_rows; default small). |

## `run-mcp-server`

Serve one index namespace to agents as read-only MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools: kg_search, kg_answer, kg_get_entity, kg_neighbors and kg_describe_schema. Needs the mcp extra

Guide: [MCP server](../guides/mcp.md). Also takes the [provider flags](#provider-flags).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--suffix` | — | Index namespace (suffix) to serve (default: the config's processing.document_parsing.index_value, else 'default'); a tool call may name another only if mcp.allowed_namespaces lists it. |
| `--transport` | `stdio` | stdio (default): the agent starts this command and talks over its stdin and stdout. streamable-http: a stateless HTTP endpoint at http://HOST:PORT/mcp. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address the HTTP transport binds (default 127.0.0.1, this machine only); a non-loopback address needs --allow-remote. |
| `--port` | `8000` | Port of the HTTP transport (default 8000). |
| `--allow-remote` | off | Let the HTTP transport bind a non-loopback address. The server authenticates no caller: put it behind a proxy or gateway that authenticates every request, and keep the port unreachable otherwise. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |

## `run-console`

Local web console: ask, ingest, evaluate, explore the graph, see usage and cost, edit the configuration

Guide: [Console](../guides/console.md).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--source-directory` | — | Workspace the console reads corpora and datasets from, and writes uploads to (its uploads/ folder); the page reads and writes nothing outside it, the cache directory and the evaluation outputs, and Settings saves a config path elsewhere only once confirmed (default: the working directory). |
| `--cache-directory` | — | Directory of the ingestion jobs' pipeline caches and of the console's own records (console/: questions asked, jobs, their logs) (default: cache). |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address to bind (default 127.0.0.1). Any other needs --allow-remote; the console has no login, so put an authenticating reverse proxy in front of it. |
| `--port` | `8501` | Port to bind (default 8501; 0 picks a free one). |
| `--allow-remote` | off | Allow a --host other than a loopback address. Anyone who can reach the port can then query, ingest and edit the configuration. |
| `--trace-url` `TEMPLATE` | — | Link each answer to its trace: a URL with {trace_id}, e.g. http://localhost:16686/trace/{trace_id} for Jaeger (default with observability.backend langfuse: LANGFUSE_HOST/trace/{trace_id}). |
| `--config-path` | — | Configuration YAML file (without one: the built-in defaults and the UKR__ environment variables); a missing file is a usage error. |
| `--allow-unknown-keys` | off | Ignore config keys (and UKR__ environment variables) the configuration does not define, with a warning each, instead of failing: the load fails on one by default, since a misspelled key would leave its setting at the default. |
| `--output-format` | `text` | 'text' (default) for people; 'json' prints one JSON result to stdout (for a run that failed or was stopped before it, a status with the exit code and the error) and everything else to stderr. |
| `--log-level` | — | Log level of this run (default: logging.level, INFO; DEBUG logs hold user and corpus text). With --output-format text the logs are plain lines unless logging.log_format is set. One of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`. |
| `--version` | — | Print the version and exit. |

## Provider flags

Taken by `run-ingestion`, `run-rag`, `run-eval`, `run-describe`, `run-prompt-tuning`, `prepare-benchmark assertions`, `run-mcp-server`. Override the config's provider selection (see docs/guides/local-mode.md).

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--backend` | — | Provider preset: 'aws' (Bedrock, Neptune, OpenSearch, DynamoDB) or 'local' (Ollama, cross-encoder, embedded SQLite stores). The preset fills in only keys the config leaves unset: a providers.*, models.*, aws.neptune.* or aws.opensearch.* key the file sets always wins. --backend aws over a 'backend: local' file drops the values the local preset filled in (those keys return to the AWS defaults); a value the file or the environment sets is kept. |
| `--llm-provider` `KIND` | — | providers.llm.kind: bedrock, openai_compatible or ollama. |
| `--llm-model` `MODEL` | — | models.default (the default tier's language model). |
| `--embedding-provider` `KIND` | — | providers.embedding.kind: bedrock, openai_compatible or ollama. |
| `--embedding-model` `MODEL` | — | models.embedding.model_id. |
| `--embedding-dimension` `N` | — | models.embedding.dimension. |
| `--rerank-provider` `KIND` | — | providers.rerank.kind: bedrock, cross_encoder or none. |
| `--model-base-url` `URL` | — | providers.llm.base_url and providers.embedding.base_url (the Ollama or OpenAI-compatible server). |
